routes.description: Establish Christian theism through a cumulative inference from cosmic origin and order, biological complexity, mind-independent logic and mathematics, objective moral obligation, human purpose, religious experience, and the character of Jesus.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the relevant features of reality are better explained by a transcendent personal mind than by atheistic naturalism, and connect that mind to the Christian conception of God strongly enough to establish the motion.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative inference to the existence of the personal God asserted by Christian theism.

centralBridges.description: Establish that cosmic origin, physical intelligibility, fine-tuning, or biological information materially support an intelligent source.
Establish that mind-independent logic, mathematics, reason, and moral obligation require or favor a transcendent personal ground.
Provide a warranted step from a transcendent source to the Christian God through Jesus, the cross, or distinctively Christian claims.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why theistic grounding accounts for altruism, human value, purpose, and flourishing better than the proposed naturalistic accounts.
Specify how personal experience may support commitment while allowing that divine reasons can exceed human knowledge.

routes.description: Defeat the inference to God by enforcing the claimant's evidential burden, defending methodological naturalism, supplying non-theistic accounts of the disputed phenomena, and challenging Christian revelation and religious experience.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the pro considerations neither require nor reliably identify a deity, that available naturalistic explanations block the asserted inferences, and that faith, revelation, and experience do not provide independently verifiable grounds for the motion.

motionBridge.description: Connect the unmet evidential burden and defeated identification inferences to nonestablishment of the asserted God's existence.

centralBridges.description: Require the party asserting God to provide testable or independently verifiable support beyond faith and unsupported supernatural addition.
Show that evolution, constrained natural processes, social morality, and finite human meaning do not require divine causation.
Show that conflicting experiences, religious diversity, scriptural problems, and Christian doctrines undermine reliable identification of the proposed God.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test design claims against inefficient biological complexity, evolutionary mechanisms, and the explanatory limits of invoking supernatural agency.
Explain why absent reliable divine disclosure supports warranted nonbelief rather than shifting responsibility to the skeptic.

sections.title: Evidence, Burden, and Methodological Naturalism
sections.rationale: The debate turns first on what evidence an existence claim requires, whether faith or personal certainty can supply knowledge, and whether supernatural explanation adds testable information.

sections.title: Cosmic Origin, Physical Order, and Design
sections.rationale: Claims about the universe's beginning, comprehensibility, physical laws, fine-tuning, and constrained natural processes form a distinct clash over whether cosmic features warrant an originating mind.

sections.title: Biological Complexity, Evolution, and Intelligent Design
sections.rationale: Cellular information, irreducible complexity, evolutionary accumulation, inefficient mechanisms, and endosymbiosis bear directly on whether living systems support intelligent design.

sections.title: Logic, Mathematics, and Rational Order
sections.rationale: The status of mind-independent logical and mathematical truths tests whether immaterial rational order requires a transcendent mind or remains true without divine grounding.

sections.title: Morality, Human Value, Purpose, and Altruism
sections.rationale: Objective obligation, human worth, costly assistance, social cooperation, finite meaning, and flourishing comprise the central dispute over what theism and naturalism can ground.

sections.title: Christian Revelation, Religious Experience, and Hiddenness
sections.rationale: Jesus, the cross, scripture, conflicting religious experiences, religious diversity, and absent public verification determine whether a general theistic inference can be identified with Christianity.

routes.description: Establish a cumulative inference from the existence and character of physical reality, rationality, biological information, moral obligation, evil, and scientific order to a transcendent, intelligent, personal, morally perfect, and sustaining divine cause.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the cited features require or are better accounted for by the attributes of a theistic God, that skeptical naturalism does not supply adequate grounding for those features, and that the cumulative explanation remains coherent under objections from suffering and scientific alternatives.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative explanatory force of creation, reason, information, morality, evil, and science to the conclusion that God is the best overall explanation of reality.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the beginning, composition, and fine-tuned conditions of physical reality require a cause transcending space, time, and matter and possessing sufficient power and intelligence.
Explain why reliable reason, law-governed natural order, and message-like biological information require an intelligent source rather than being adequately grounded in unguided material processes.
Establish that objective moral truths and obligations require an external, unchanging standard grounded in a personal divine nature rather than solely in human preference or social development.
Reconcile suffering and wrongdoing with the proposed divine attributes while explaining how recognition of evil and the demand for ultimate justice depend on objective goodness.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that evolutionary mechanisms operating on existing life do not by themselves explain the origin of replication, genetic coding, epigenetic organization, or the first living system.
Demonstrate that the attributes inferred across the separate explanatory domains converge on one coherent theistic cause rather than an unrelated collection of causes.

routes.description: Defend evidence-sensitive suspension of theistic belief and present scientific inquiry, natural mechanisms, emergent human capacities, and human-centered ethics as sufficient methods and resources for explaining the relevant features of reality.
routes.successCriteria: Establish a public and testable evidential standard, show that invoking God does not add a supported mechanism or discriminating prediction, provide naturalistic accounts where the theistic case alleges explanatory dependence, and identify observations that burden the proposed divine explanation.

motionBridge.description: Connect testable, revisable, and publicly checkable inquiry to the conclusion that skeptical naturalism is warranted over an insufficiently evidenced theistic explanation.

centralBridges.description: Establish that explanatory claims require publicly assessable evidence, mechanisms, and exposure to possible disconfirmation rather than belief, private experience, or appeals to unresolved gaps.
Show that physical, evolutionary, and emergent processes can account for biological information, complexity, thought, choice, and rational practice without requiring a supernatural source.
Ground moral judgment, objective standards, purpose, and progress in shared human nature, harm reduction, empathy, reciprocity, relationships, social learning, and revisable institutions.
Show that extensive preventable suffering and an inhospitable cosmic history create evidential difficulty for an all-knowing, all-powerful, wholly good, human-directed creator.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require a reliable evidential procedure for distinguishing Christianity or theism from incompatible religious alternatives and inherited or experiential commitments.
Explain how organized criticism, replication, and attention to selection effects make scientific inquiry capable of correcting cognitive biases behind apparent design, providence, and miracles.

sections.title: Evidence, Testability, and Explanatory Adequacy
sections.rationale: This issue establishes what must count as an explanation of reality, including the roles of causal inference, mechanisms, testability, cumulative argument, skeptical withholding of belief, and scientific self-correction.

sections.title: Cosmic Origins, Fine-Tuning, and Transcendent Causation
sections.rationale: This section addresses whether the universe’s beginning, physical conditions, and apparent order warrant a transcendent intelligent cause or remain open to naturalistic alternatives and non-purposeful cosmic history.

sections.title: Biological Information, Life’s Origin, and Evolution
sections.rationale: This issue joins the inference from genetic and organismal information to intelligence with disputes over evolutionary mechanisms, genomic history, thermodynamics, abiogenesis, replication, and biological organization.

sections.title: Reason, Mind, Freedom, and the Order Presupposed by Science
sections.rationale: This section concerns whether rational thought, volition, and stable natural order require a divine rational ground or can arise and remain trustworthy within physical and emergent naturalistic accounts.

sections.title: Moral Grounding, Human Meaning, and Justice
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether objective moral duties, human purpose, and ultimate justice require God’s nature and judgment or can be grounded in human nature, empathy, social development, relationships, and institutions.

sections.title: Evil, Divine Purpose, and Competing Religious Claims
sections.rationale: This section addresses whether suffering and religious diversity fit a purposeful, good God and a specifically Christian account, or instead support evidential skepticism about providence, revelation, miracles, and exclusive truth claims.

routes.description: Establish that the morally relevant form of hell is freely sustained separation from God and internally arising degeneration, with divine justice correcting honest error, grace enabling escape, and annihilation remaining possible instead of externally inflicted endless torture.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it connects culpable persistence in separation to its suffering, preserves a genuine and accessible path of rescue for willing or honestly mistaken souls, and explains duration, destruction, and atonement consistently with perfect justice and love.

motionBridge.description: Show that self-chosen exile, sanctifying grace, and possible annihilation jointly provide a morally coherent Christian account of hell distinct from externally imposed eternal torture.

centralBridges.description: Establish that some rejection of God can remain informed, attributable, and voluntarily sustained despite psychological and social influences on belief.
Explain hellish suffering as the internal consequence of persistent sin, pride, and separation rather than an externally administered torture regime.
Require adequate correction for honest misinformation and an effective offer of grace capable of carrying every willing soul through painful sanctification.
Account for proportionality by permitting departure upon repentance, possible universal salvation, or eventual annihilation rather than necessary endless confinement.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how Christ's death, exile, resurrection, and experienced rupture supply the theological basis for rescue from sin and separation.
Distinguish inherited punitive imagery from the defended doctrine while identifying a non-retaliatory role for confidence in just divine judgment.

routes.description: Establish that continued hell cannot be morally justified as freely chosen when rejection is produced by involuntary conviction, misinformation, incapacity, or circumstances, and that prolonged suffering, annihilation, or an inadequately grounded rescue mechanism remains ethically problematic.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the alleged choice of hell is reduced to preventable error or impaired agency, the available escape conditions imply rescue or universalism rather than warranted persistence, or the duration, severity, and salvific basis cannot meet proportionality and loving-correction requirements.

motionBridge.description: Show that redescribing hell as exile, sanctification, or annihilation does not justify suffering or destruction unless continued separation is informed, voluntary, proportionate, and unavoidable by a perfectly loving God.

centralBridges.description: Establish that belief and rejection arise from evidence, experience, psychology, and circumstances that do not become morally culpable merely because identity or bias is involved.
Require a perfectly loving and powerful God to correct misinformation and provide sufficient clarification before permitting harmful separation or fixing a soul's fate.
Show that a soul remaining in hell is either unable to leave, mistaken about the alternatives, or willing to seek rescue, undermining informed voluntary exile.
Test whether prolonged suffering, irreversible loss, or annihilation can be proportionate to finite wrongdoing or belief formed without adequate control.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Trace whether universal access to correction and grace leaves any morally permissible case in which a soul permanently remains separated from God.
Test whether Christ undergoes the consequence assigned to sinners and whether the asserted sacrifice is proportionate to the rescue it is invoked to secure.

sections.title: Nature and authorship of hellish suffering
sections.rationale: The motion turns first on whether hell is externally inflicted punishment or an internally generated condition of sin, pride, separation, degeneration, and possible destruction. That distinction defines what requires moral justification.

sections.title: Agency, information, and culpable rejection
sections.rationale: The self-chosen-exile account depends on whether rejection of God can be informed and morally attributable despite involuntary conviction, misinformation, motivated reasoning, identity, experience, and subconscious influence.

sections.title: Duration, escape, annihilation, and proportionality
sections.rationale: Possible release and annihilation answer objections to everlasting torture only if the remaining suffering or destruction is proportionate and if no external barrier prevents a willing soul from leaving.

sections.title: Grace, painful sanctification, and universalism
sections.rationale: Grace is the proposed answer to moral incapacity, while painful sanctification explains resistance to rescue. Their interaction determines whether continued exile remains possible or adequate correction and mercy instead entail universal salvation.

sections.title: Atonement and the basis of rescue
sections.rationale: The offered route out of hell relies on Christ's treatment of sin's consequences. The nature of death and exile, the adequacy of substitution, and the proportional significance of the crucifixion therefore materially support the broader moral account.

routes.description: Show that the cited facts about pain, pleasure, languishing, and horrendous evil do not provide comparative evidence for naturalism over theism because the naturalistic likelihood is not established, soul-building can raise their likelihood on theism, or skeptical theism prevents the required likelihood comparison.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if at least one global neutralizer defeats the comparative inference: the naturalistic prediction remains unsupported, a sufficiently developed soul-building account makes the data no less expected on theism, or epistemic limits leave the theistic likelihood unavailable for the claimed comparison.

motionBridge.description: Establish that the total cited suffering data do not warrant a comparative evidential preference for naturalism over theism.

centralBridges.description: Require adequate support for the claim that naturalism predicts the observed suffering facts better, rather than merely accommodating their possibility.
Explain how morally significant agency, virtue formation, nonhuman development, and eventual defeat of suffering can make the observed data compatible with theistic purposes.
Show that limited access to divine reasons or the total moral structure prevents a warranted estimate of the suffering data's probability on theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test whether the biological analogy and selected evolutionary background information support the asserted naturalistic expectations.
Address whether less harmful means, afterlife compensation, or the destructive effects of suffering undermine the proposed theistic purposes.

routes.description: Show that biologically oriented pain and pleasure, widespread sentient languishing, and horrendous evil are collectively more expected on morally indifferent naturalism than on theism, and that neither soul-building nor skeptical theism neutralizes that comparative evidential force.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by defending the comparative-likelihood standard, establishing a naturalistic advantage for the principal classes of suffering facts, and showing that soul-building and skeptical-theist replies neither predict the observed distribution nor erase the force of known evidence.

motionBridge.description: Establish that the total cited suffering data provide comparative evidential support for naturalism over theism.

centralBridges.description: Defend the principle that evidence favors the hypothesis on which the observed facts are less surprising, without requiring either hypothesis to entail them.
Establish a comparative naturalistic advantage for biologically oriented pain and pleasure, sentient languishing, and horrendous evil.
Show that soul-building does not adequately predict the scope, distribution, proportions, or destructive severity of the observed suffering.
Show that uncertainty about unknown divine reasons does not cancel known comparative reasons or prevent naturalism from assigning the data a higher likelihood.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify background knowledge without building the disputed suffering observations into it or requiring an independent complete naturalistic explanation.
Explain why less harmful means, divine resources, compensation, or possible afterlives do not by themselves justify or predict the observed harms.

sections.title: Comparative Likelihood and Naturalistic Prediction
sections.rationale: This issue fixes the governing evidential standard and whether analogical reasoning, evolutionary background knowledge, and comparative surprise adequately support a naturalistic likelihood advantage.

sections.title: Biological Orientation of Pain and Pleasure
sections.rationale: The orientation of pain and pleasure toward biological goals, and its apparent moral randomness, forms an independent evidential comparison that each side must explain under its hypothesis.

sections.title: Sentient Flourishing and Languishing
sections.rationale: The prevalence, distribution, and nonhuman scope of languishing test whether natural processes or theistic purposes better predict the observed proportions of sentient welfare.

sections.title: Horrendous Evil and Divine Prevention
sections.rationale: The severity, morally destructive effects, and apparent preventability of horrendous evil create a distinct comparison involving divine empathy, available alternatives, and indifferent natural processes.

sections.title: Scope and Necessity of Soul-Building
sections.rationale: Soul-building is a principal global neutralizer, so the debate must address its reach across humans and animals, the necessity of actual harms, freedom, afterlife defeat, and any claimed fine-tuning.

sections.title: Skeptical Theism and Unknown Reasons
sections.rationale: The final global issue is whether limited human access to divine reasons makes the theistic likelihood unknowable or whether known comparative evidence remains probative despite that uncertainty.

routes.description: Establish that Jesus personally claimed divine identity by reading his titles, sayings, prerogatives, and reception cumulatively within a first-century Jewish two-powers framework and by defending that interpretation against delegated-authority alternatives.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the relevant Jewish framework can include distinguishable divine figures, Jesus applies that identity framework to himself through words and functions, and the cumulative evidence is not adequately explained by mere agency, exalted humanity, or later attribution.

motionBridge.description: Connect Jesus's own claimed titles, authority, and functions to personal participation in divine identity rather than merely to later beliefs about him.

centralBridges.description: Establish that Jewish scripture supplied a recognizable framework of distinguishable figures sharing Yahweh's identity and that Jesus located himself within it.
Show that Jesus's Son, Lord, Son of Man, divine-name, unity, and preexistence language communicates more than messianic or representative status.
Show that Jesus's claims to equal honor, universal judgment, life-giving authority, resurrection power, and premundane glory identify him with divine functions.
Connect followers' devotion and opponents' accusations to Jesus's self-claims while establishing that the resulting high christology is early rather than a late development.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how receiving authority, serving, and distinguishing himself from the Father can coexist with prior divine identity through incarnation and exaltation.
Establish when worship language and hostile reactions reliably corroborate the intended force of Jesus's claims.

routes.description: Defeat the claim that Jesus personally identified himself as God by showing that the cited language, functions, and honors remain explicable through divine name-bearing, delegated agency, messianic or ideal-human status, and later high christology.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative cannot bridge from disputed texts and received authority to Jesus's own divine identity because viable agency readings remain, contrary dependence language persists, or early Christian portrayals do not establish Jesus's historical self-claim.

motionBridge.description: Show that exalted status, divine authorization, name-bearing, or later portrayal does not by itself establish that Jesus personally claimed to be God.

centralBridges.description: Establish that Jewish representatives could bear God's name, exercise transmitted authority, and receive deference without being identical with Yahweh.
Show that unity, glory, judgment, forgiveness, miraculous power, and other assertedly divine features are received by Jesus or extended to disciples.
Provide non-divine readings of the principal Johannine, Synoptic, Danielic, and Pauline terms and passages used to infer divine identity.
Separate claims made by Jesus from followers' devotion, authorial framing, later high christology, and historically disputed interpretations.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that blasphemy accusations, stoning attempts, and other reactions may reflect misunderstanding or charges that do not require a divine-identity claim.
Distinguish homage language applicable to non-divine recipients from cultic service that would uniquely identify its recipient as God.

sections.title: Two powers, divine name-bearing, and Jewish agency
sections.rationale: This issue supplies the controlling historical framework for deciding whether distinguishable Yahweh figures and divine name-bearing imply shared divine identity or delegated representation.

sections.title: Jesus's sayings, titles, and scriptural allusions
sections.rationale: The motion centrally depends on whether Son, Lord, Son of Man, unity, preexistence, and divine-name language constitutes Jesus's personal divine claim or permits non-divine readings.

sections.title: Divine prerogatives, dependence, and delegated authority
sections.rationale: Claims involving judgment, resurrection, life, forgiveness, glory, and Sabbath authority must be tested against language of receipt, dependence, prayer, and comparable grants to disciples.

sections.title: Worship, early devotion, and hostile reactions
sections.rationale: Followers' prayers and homage and opponents' blasphemy reactions may corroborate Jesus's intended claim, but their semantic force and reliability require independent assessment.

sections.title: Historical self-claim and christological development
sections.rationale: The debate requires separating Jesus's own claims from Gospel framing and early Christian christology while assessing Synoptic and Johannine differences, Pauline material, and proposed development.

routes.description: Establish that contemporary cosmology supports neutral premises concerning a finite cosmic past and fine-tuned initial conditions, then connect those premises through causal and design reasoning to a transcendent personal creator.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if cosmological evidence makes a beginning and purposive fine-tuning sufficiently credible, naturalistic alternatives do not remove their explanatory force, and the resulting causal and design inferences make God's existence more probable.

motionBridge.description: Show that the relevant cosmological evidence raises the probability of a transcendent creator and designer.

centralBridges.description: Establish that expansion, thermodynamics, and the limits of proposed eternal models favor an ultimate cosmic beginning.
Establish that a universe beginning to exist requires a cause beyond physical spacetime and that personal agency can account for a finite effect.
Establish that life-permitting constants and low initial entropy are improbable without design and are more expected under theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify theoretical, thermodynamic, and observer-typicality difficulties confronting beginningless or multiverse alternatives.
Maintain the distinction between cosmology supplying neutral premises and philosophical arguments drawing the theistic conclusion.

routes.description: Establish that self-contained naturalistic cosmological models can account for a finite or eternal universe, while theistic explanations lack constrained observational expectations and add no required explanatory element.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if neither a cosmic boundary nor fine-tuning requires a transcendent agent, viable naturalistic models remain available, and comparative explanatory standards favor constrained, self-contained accounts over an underdetermined theistic explanation.

motionBridge.description: Show that naturalistic cosmological models explain the universe without making God's existence more probable.

centralBridges.description: Establish that singularity results do not prove an absolute beginning and that coherent finite or eternal models need no external cause.
Establish that causal concepts grounded within spacetime need not apply to the universe as a whole or to a first temporal boundary.
Establish that fine-tuning probabilities are measure-dependent and that naturalistic principles or multiverse models can address observed conditions.
Require competing explanations to generate constrained expectations and show how self-contained naturalism can meet that requirement.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Treat low entropy and observer typicality as model-dependent research problems rather than direct evidence of divine design.
Apply parsimony and explanatory self-containment when an invisible creator adds no distinct observational consequences.

sections.title: Cosmic Beginning and Eternal Models
sections.rationale: Whether contemporary expansion results, singularity theorems, thermodynamics, and quantum cosmologies favor an ultimate beginning is a principal empirical premise in the cosmological argument.

sections.title: Causation, Time, and a First Moment
sections.rationale: The inference from a temporal boundary to a transcendent personal cause depends on whether causation applies to the universe and how temporal becoming and first moments are understood.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning and Cosmological Probability
sections.rationale: The design inference requires defensible probability measures, genuinely restricted life-permitting conditions, and a justified comparison of those observations under theism and naturalism.

sections.title: Low Entropy, Multiverses, and Observer Typicality
sections.rationale: Low initial entropy and the prevalence of ordinary observers test whether multiverse or equilibrium models provide an adequate naturalistic alternative to purposive design.

sections.title: Explanatory Scope and Predictive Standards
sections.rationale: The motion-level comparison depends on whether theism functions as an evidential conclusion from neutral premises and whether either worldview supplies constrained, parsimonious observational expectations.

routes.description: Establish Christian theism as the more adequate account of cosmic intelligibility, rational knowledge, objective morality, human dignity, and enduring hope, while connecting those explanatory claims to the character and revelation of the Christian God.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its general theistic explanations remain coherent under naturalistic objections, its specifically Christian claims have an adequate epistemic bridge, and its account of divine greatness addresses evil, coercion, and religious wrongdoing.

motionBridge.description: Show that the Christian God is worthy of the motion's greatness claim and that Christian theism jointly explains the motion's scientific, moral, dignitary, and hopeful dimensions better than anti-theism.

centralBridges.description: Account for cosmic order, biological information, and trustworthy rational inquiry through an intelligent creator without treating scientific mechanisms as competing creator explanations.
Ground objective moral obligation and distinctive human worth in God rather than in wholly blind natural processes.
Supply a warranted transition from general creator claims to Christianity through claims about Jesus, revelation, resurrection, and atonement.
Reconcile divine greatness with suffering, judgment, freedom, and allegations that supernatural authority is intrinsically tyrannical.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish conduct that follows Christian teaching from violence or oppression committed by professed adherents contrary to that teaching.
Relate Christian commitments to liberty, conscience, rights, education, and reform without making historical association substitute for the central truth claims.

routes.description: Defeat the claimed explanatory and moral advantages of Christian theism by advancing naturalistic and secular alternatives, challenging the evidential bridge to revelation, and arguing that the proposed divine rule is neither necessary nor worthy of worship.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if natural and human explanations cover the motion's principal domains without God, specifically Christian claims remain insufficiently warranted, and suffering, authority, atonement, or religion's effects defeat the attribution of divine greatness.

motionBridge.description: Show that Christian theism neither provides the better explanation across the motion's domains nor establishes a God whose character and governance satisfy the claim of greatness.

centralBridges.description: Defend evidence-responsive natural inquiry and show that adding divine agency does not improve explanations of cosmic or biological phenomena.
Explain morality, solidarity, dignity, meaning, and hope through human social, evolutionary, intellectual, and cultural resources without supernatural premises.
Require adequate evidence for knowledge of divine intentions and contest the historical, prophetic, and miraculous basis of specifically Christian revelation.
Show how suffering, surveillance, punishment, coercion, or vicarious redemption conflicts with the asserted goodness and greatness of the Christian God.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Establish whether religious violence and oppression arise from supernatural doctrines themselves rather than merely from their misuse.
Test claims of Christian moral or political progress against religious complicity, nonreligious reform, and competing explanations of totalitarianism.

sections.title: Cosmic Intelligibility, Biology, and Natural Explanation
sections.rationale: This issue tests the motion's science dimension by comparing creator-based explanations of order, intelligibility, and biological information with naturalistic standards of evidence and explanatory sufficiency.

sections.title: Reason, Revelation, and the Warrant for Christianity
sections.rationale: The motion concerns Christian theism rather than an unspecified first cause, making the epistemic transition from cosmic order to divine intentions, Jesus's identity, miracles, prophecy, and resurrection indispensable.

sections.title: Morality, Objective Obligation, and Atonement
sections.rationale: This section addresses whether God is required to ground moral truth and responsibility, whether secular accounts can sustain moral judgment, and whether distinctively Christian sacrifice coheres morally.

sections.title: Human Dignity, Meaning, Solidarity, and Hope
sections.rationale: The issue directly covers three named burdens by testing divine-image and ultimate-hope accounts against evolutionary, social, cultural, and secular accounts of human worth and purpose.

sections.title: Divine Greatness, Suffering, Freedom, and Authority
sections.rationale: Because the motion expressly asks whether God is great, the implications of natural evil, judgment, omniscience, freedom, redemption, and divine governance form a distinct motion-level clash.

sections.title: Religion, Violence, Liberty, and Historical Consequences
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether coercion and social harm follow from Christian or supernatural commitments and how claims about rights, reform, slavery, fascism, and totalitarianism bear on religion's consequences.

routes.description: Establish that the principal immaterial, ordered, rational, informational, moral, and purposive features of reality require an adequate grounding cause, and that their cumulative implications identify a transcendent personal creator more completely than materialist atheism does.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the relevant features of reality are shown to require foundations unavailable to materialist atheism, the proposed theistic ground accounts for them coherently, and objections concerning inferential gaps and evil do not sever the cumulative inference.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative explanatory requirements of reality to a transcendent, intelligent, moral, and personal creator, thereby establishing theism as the fuller account.

centralBridges.description: Show that the universe's beginning, contingency, and order require a cause beyond space, time, and matter rather than an unexplained natural origin.
Show that rational inference, biological information, and the presuppositions of science require immaterial and intelligent foundations that material processes alone do not supply.
Show that objective duties, rights, and judgments of good and evil require an authoritative standard beyond individuals and changing societies.
Reconcile divine power and goodness with suffering through freedom, the distinction between knowledge and causation, epistemic limits, and the possibility of wider goods or justice.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish causal and design inferences drawn from asserted positive features from an appeal that merely inserts God wherever present knowledge is incomplete.
Connect human agency and the stable operation of natural laws to a sustaining personal ground rather than exclusively determined molecular activity.

routes.description: Establish that disciplined natural inquiry, provisional uncertainty, evolutionary and social explanations, and direct human responsibility account for the relevant evidence without positing an unverified supernatural being, while testing the internal coherence of the proposed theistic explanation.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if natural and human-centered accounts remain adequate to the disputed phenomena, supernatural conclusions exceed the available evidential warrant, and the proposed divine attributes create unresolved explanatory problems rather than supplying a necessary ground.

motionBridge.description: Connect evidential restraint, natural explanation, and human ownership of moral choice to atheism's claimed superiority as an account of reality.

centralBridges.description: Show that conclusions about supernatural origins go beyond verified evidence and that acknowledged uncertainty is preferable to filling unresolved questions with divine agency.
Explain apparent cosmic and biological design through observer selection, local habitability, gradual evolution, and natural processes without inferring intentional arrangement.
Ground moral judgment, empathy, and responsibility in social decision-making and evolved cooperative capacities without requiring an objective divine lawgiver.
Show that apparently needless suffering, divine foreknowledge, and divine control of initial conditions challenge the joint claims of omnipotence, omniscience, and benevolence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require theism to explain how a law-transcending cause operates and why assigning divine attributes adds explanatory content rather than relocating unanswered questions.
Test whether religious chronology and interpretive claims independently predict discoveries or are revised after natural inquiry establishes contrary evidence.

sections.title: Cosmic origin, fine-tuning, and supernatural inference
sections.rationale: This issue contains the principal clash over whether the universe's beginning and apparent calibration warrant a transcendent cause or instead require evidential restraint, observer-selection analysis, and continued natural inquiry.

sections.title: Reason, biological information, evolution, and science
sections.rationale: This issue tests competing accounts of rational reliability, DNA information, apparent biological design, and the conceptual foundations of scientific inquiry, all of which bear directly on each worldview's explanatory reach.

sections.title: Moral standards, empathy, and human responsibility
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether moral obligation requires a transcendent objective standard or can arise through social judgment, evolved empathy, and human ownership of choices, making it central to both stated burdens.

sections.title: Evil, suffering, freedom, and divine attributes
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether evil supports an objective moral ground, can be reconciled with a good and powerful creator, or instead renders the proposed divine attributes internally difficult to sustain.

sections.title: Comparative explanation, falsifiability, and epistemic method
sections.rationale: This issue integrates the motion-level dispute over positive inference, gaps reasoning, falsifiability, honest uncertainty, religious adaptation, and what each side must provide for its account to qualify as the better explanation.

moves.speaker: Frank Turek
moves.proposition: Theism better explains reality because reality includes immaterial aspects that materialist atheism cannot account for.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly hands the opening statement to Turek, whose uninterrupted first-person presentation continues through this window.

response.rationale: This constructive thesis states the motion-level comparison and organizes the later case around allegedly immaterial features of reality.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly frames the proposed cumulative route and comparative conclusion.

precisionFindings.rationale: The thesis is recoverable, but “immaterial aspects” and the scope of materialist atheism are not carefully delimited.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The categorical claim that atheism cannot be true precedes the supporting arguments and exceeds what the thesis statement itself establishes.

charity.alternative: Materialism may recognize abstract descriptions or emergent mental properties without treating them as separate substances.
charity.decisiveQualification: Recognizing immaterial descriptions is not itself a complete materialist account of their grounding.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The adjudicated raw ledger applies the preregistered rounded mean to the two nondisputed logicalCoherence values (72 and 68); their difference did not meet a semantic or magnitude dispute trigger.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: This span asserts the comparative thesis but supplies no representative support or comparison of competing explanations.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It expressly advances the motion bridge by claiming theism is the better cumulative explanation of reality.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move largely treats materialist atheism as simply denying every immaterial aspect and does not engage emergentist alternatives.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt contrasts materialist atheism with a theistic account and expressly makes immaterial reality the basis of the better-explanation thesis.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it directly develops an indispensable central bridge with an explicit causal inference.

calibrationFindings.rationale: A transcendent cause is presented as necessary, while the additional inference to an intelligent creator is more compressed than that force suggests.

charity.alternative: A natural origin model might deny that ordinary temporal causation applies to the universe as a whole.
charity.decisiveQualification: Such a model must still explain why spacetime and matter exist or begin without merely assuming the disputed origin.

moves.speaker: Frank Turek
moves.proposition: Materialist atheism undermines trust in reason because unguided molecular processes provide neither free rational choice nor warranted beliefs.
moves.attributionBasis: Turek explicitly introduces reason as his second line of evidence and remains the sole speaker throughout the complete argument.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it supplies a clear central argument, though its determinism-to-unreliability bridge is compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The argument is recoverable, but “molecular machines,” reaction, reasoning, and trust shift between causal and epistemic senses without qualification.

calibrationFindings.rationale: It treats material causation as necessarily eliminating reasoning and warrant without addressing compatibilist or reliability-based accounts.

charity.alternative: Materially caused cognitive processes can still implement valid reasoning and produce generally reliable beliefs.
charity.decisiveQualification: Causal determination alone does not establish epistemic unreliability or the absence of reason-responsive cognition.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The argument relies on unsupported conditionals from material causation to no free will, from no free will to no reasoning, and then to distrust.

routes.description: Reconcile a loving and powerful God with suffering by identifying morally sufficient reasons for permitting evil, limits on human inference from unexplained suffering, and the roles of freedom, stable natural order, and religiously grounded moral response.
routes.successCriteria: Establish that suffering does not defeat theistic belief if divine permission can be coherently connected to morally significant freedom, life-supporting regularities, limited human knowledge, and a constructive account of humanity's obligations toward sufferers.

motionBridge.description: Show that the scale of suffering remains logically and evidentially compatible with a loving, powerful God when permission can serve morally sufficient purposes.

centralBridges.description: Show that inability to identify God's reason for a particular instance of suffering does not establish that no sufficient reason exists.
Explain why morally significant human freedom can require permitting consequential choices, including choices that produce grave moral evil.
Explain why stable, life-supporting natural conditions can entail dangerous processes and why routine intervention could compromise consequential agency.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Connect humanity's demand for autonomy with a world in which freedom operates through stable consequences and exposure to suffering.
Account for how theistic belief can widen moral concern and motivate practical service to people experiencing suffering.

routes.description: Challenge the survival of belief by arguing that immense innocent suffering, inconsistent or inadequate explanations, and the absence of expected divine intervention make the world unlike one governed by an all-loving and all-powerful God.
routes.successCriteria: Establish that the quantity, distribution, and apparent preventability of suffering remain insufficiently explained by freedom, natural-law necessity, or mystery, while conflicting with scriptural expectations of compassionate divine intervention.

motionBridge.description: Show that pervasive, apparently preventable suffering counts strongly against the existence of the loving, powerful, interventionist God under discussion.

centralBridges.description: Demonstrate that innocent and extreme suffering resists explanations based on punishment, deserved consequences, or morally proportionate outcomes.
Establish a discrepancy between scriptural portrayals of divine rescue and healing and the apparent absence of comparable intervention amid present suffering.
Test whether appeals to freedom, natural necessity, or human ignorance actually explain the scale and distribution of suffering without internal inconsistency.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that divergent biblical explanations complicate any claim that scripture supplies a unified and adequate account of suffering.
Provide a non-theistic basis for compassion, consolation, and practical efforts to reduce suffering without treating those responses as evidence for God.

sections.title: Divine Love, Power, and Expected Intervention
sections.rationale: This is the motion-level clash over whether massive, apparently preventable suffering is compatible with divine love and power, especially where scripture depicts an active God who intervenes.

sections.title: Epistemic Limits and Scriptural Explanations
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether limited human understanding and biblical treatments of suffering preserve possible divine reasons or instead leave incompatible and inadequate explanations.

sections.title: Human Freedom and Moral Evil
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether morally significant freedom supplies a sufficient reason to permit atrocities and whether extreme human wrongdoing fits either theistic or naturalistic explanation.

sections.title: Natural Law, Fine-Tuning, and Natural Suffering
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether dangerous natural processes are necessary features of a stable, life-supporting universe or conditions an omnipotent creator could have arranged differently.

sections.title: Meaning, Compassion, and Responses to Suffering
sections.rationale: This issue concerns whether religious belief distinctively explains or enlarges concern for sufferers, and whether secular accounts can ground compassion and practical relief independently.
